title: The last Tuesday of summer
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Tuesday. The shop. The owner says summer's done — the tourists' photos stop coming in the week the school buses start. She can tell the season by the counter. Wood asks what comes next. She says diplomas, then deer. He writes it on the wall under the tally.

panels.composition: The shop. The counter, empty. The OWNER at her station. WOOD at the cutter. Nothing to frame.

balloons.text: Summer's done. Photos stop the week the buses start.

image.prompt: a quiet frame shop with an empty counter, a woman at her station and a young man at a mat cutter with nothing to cut, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood, writing on the wall under the tally, in pencil: DIPLOMAS. DEER.

image.prompt: close on a young man's hand writing two words in pencil on a wall beneath tally marks, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The owner, seeing it. Not objecting.

image.prompt: a woman in reading glasses glancing at two words written on her backroom wall, not objecting, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The shop from the road. The window. The card: TUE · THU · SAT. The season turning on the counter. The strip learns the year by what comes in the door.

image.prompt: a low roadside frame shop seen from the highway with an hours card in its window at the end of summer, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'Diplomas. Then deer.' The year by the counter.
